boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Maryland-College Park, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence built around UMD landmarks, campus spaces, recreation and arts.

cards.title: Start with a campus orientation walk
cards.subtitle: University of Maryland Visitor Center · College Park
cards.notes: Begin by using UMD’s visitor resources and interactive campus map to identify buildings, landmarks and the routes you want to revisit over the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for getting oriented on the 1,350-acre campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD’s Visit page directs visitors to student-led tours, a self-guided tour and an interactive tool that identifies every campus building and parking option.
cards.access_notes: Check the Visit UMD page for current tour options and visitor information before going.

cards.title: Photograph the floral M
cards.subtitle: The M · Campus Drive
cards.notes: Pause at the large floral M on Campus Drive for an easy location marker, then continue toward the center of campus on foot.
cards.short_summary: A named UMD landmark planted with more than 850 flowers twice each year.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD identifies the giant floral M on Campus Drive as a landmark and says more than 850 flowers are planted there twice annually.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; consult the campus map for walking directions.

cards.title: Cross McKeldin Mall
cards.subtitle: McKeldin Mall · central campus
cards.notes: Walk the length of the mall from Main Administration toward McKeldin Library and use the open lawn as the spine for your first campus loop.
cards.short_summary: A 16.28-acre academic mall linking Main Administration Building and McKeldin Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD describes McKeldin Mall as a 16.28-acre area extending from Main Administration Building to McKeldin Library.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; check the campus map and any event notices before planning a gathering there.

cards.title: Meet Testudo at the library
cards.subtitle: Testudo · in front of McKeldin Library
cards.notes: Find the original bronze Testudo outside McKeldin Library and take a close look at the polished nose before continuing your campus walk.
cards.short_summary: The original 1933 bronze mascot statue stands at the heart of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD states that the bronze Testudo in front of McKeldin Library is its best-known good-luck tradition and that rubbing its nose is customary.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark in front of McKeldin Library; be considerate of other visitors using the area.

cards.entity_name: Frederick Douglass Square at Hornbake Plaza
cards.title: Visit Frederick Douglass Square
cards.subtitle: Frederick Douglass Square · Hornbake Plaza
cards.notes: Make a short detour to Hornbake Plaza to view the memorial and use it as a waypoint while learning the north-side campus paths.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor memorial centered on an eight-foot bronze statue of Frederick Douglass.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD’s visitor guide identifies Frederick Douglass Square at Hornbake Plaza as a memorial with an eight-foot bronze statue honoring Douglass.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial at Hornbake Plaza; verify the route on UMD’s interactive map.

cards.title: Get acquainted with Stamp
cards.subtitle: Adele H. Stamp Student Union · 3972 Campus Drive
cards.notes: Walk through Stamp to locate study areas, information services, galleries and the campus programs that may help shape your first few weeks.
cards.short_summary: UMD’s student union combines lounges, study space, information services, arts and entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD’s catalog says Stamp offers lounge and study areas, information services, recreation, arts and entertainment, food and retail outlets, and event space.
cards.source_title: Adele H. Stamp Student Union - Center for Campus Life
cards.access_notes: The catalog lists academic-year building hours, with modified hours during summer and university breaks.

cards.title: Try a game at TerpZone
cards.subtitle: TerpZone · basement of Stamp Student Union
cards.notes: If you want a low-key group activity, check TerpZone’s availability and choose bowling, billiards or video games that fit your group and budget.
cards.short_summary: A Stamp recreation space with bowling lanes, billiards, video games and big-screen TVs.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD’s catalog identifies TerpZone in Stamp as having bowling lanes, cosmic bowling, billiard tables, video games and three big-screen TVs.
cards.source_title: Adele H. Stamp Student Union - Center for Campus Life
cards.access_notes: Located in Stamp; check TerpZone directly for current availability and any activity charges.

cards.title: Take a quiet chapel-and-garden pause
cards.subtitle: Memorial Chapel · 7744 Regents Drive
cards.notes: Add a daytime stop at the chapel and adjacent gardens for a quieter change of pace, then continue toward the recreation and arts destinations.
cards.short_summary: A multifaith campus chapel and garden open to people of all faiths, cultures and ways of being.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Chapel says its doors are open year-round to the campus community, alumni and wider community, and welcomes all faiths, cultures and ways of being.
cards.access_notes: Posted public hours are Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; weekends are closed except for events and worship services.

cards.title: Move at Eppley Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Eppley Recreation Center · North Campus
cards.notes: For an active afternoon, check access eligibility and choose from the listed cardio, court, climbing or aquatics activities rather than committing to a full routine.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose recreation facility with cardio, courts, bouldering, swimming and group fitness options.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD lists cardio and weight training, basketball, a bouldering zone, racquetball and squash, swimming, badminton and group fitness among Eppley’s activities.
cards.access_notes: UMD states that a RecWell membership or facility rental is required; review current facility hours before visiting.

cards.title: End with an arts stop at The Clarice
cards.subtitle: Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center · campus arts district
cards.notes: Check the current calendar before you go, then use The Clarice as a final stop to identify performances, library resources and art spaces for later visits.
cards.short_summary: UMD’s performing-arts hub houses Clarice Presents, music, theatre, dance and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD identifies The Clarice as its performing-arts hub and home to Clarice Presents, the School of Music, theatre and dance programs, and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library.
cards.access_notes: Check The Clarice’s event calendar and venue guidance for current performance access or ticket requirements.
